name: Risotto alla Milanese
steps: Bring 500ml water to a boil, dissolve the stock cube and keep the broth warm on low heat throughout cooking.

Melt butter gently in a heavy-bottomed pot over low heat. Add finely diced onion and cook on the lowest setting for 10 min, stirring occasionally, until very soft and translucent — do not let it brown.
Raise heat to maximum. Add the rice and stir vigorously for 2 min until the grains toast and turn slightly darker.
Pour in the white wine and stir until the alcohol smell disappears and the liquid is fully absorbed, about 1–2 min.
Add the first ladle of hot broth and stir in the saffron. Rinse any saffron residue off the ladle into the pot. Stir until absorbed.
Continue adding broth one ladle at a time over 15 min — add the next only once the previous is absorbed. Stir regularly and keep at a gentle simmer.
When the rice is al dente and the risotto flows slowly off the spoon, remove from heat. Fold in grated Parmigiano, rest 1 min and serve immediately.
